description:
REPORTED BY USER, 2026-09-12: "You cannot force finish an exercise, you have to finish all the sets. This is restrictive for me who is sometimes on a time crunch."

Today an exercise is done only when logged sets reach targetSets. isExerciseDone (shared by SessionScreen and StartScreen, per CLAUDE.md the single source of truth) has no notion of "I stopped here on purpose". On a time crunch you either log sets you did not do, or leave the day looking unfinished forever — and because StartScreen's client-side rotation advance keys off day completion, an abandoned exercise also stalls "NEXT UP".

WANTED: a way to call an exercise finished at 2 of 4 sets, with the session honestly recording 2 sets rather than fabricating 4.

DESIGN QUESTIONS to settle before implementing:
- Where does "finished early" live? A per-(session, exercise) flag is the honest model — it belongs to today's performance, not to the program template, and not to set_log rows which record actual work. Likely a new table or a nullable column on a session-scoped row. Note there is deliberately NO session-exercise join table today (CLAUDE.md: "Exercises belong to a session iff they have >=1 logged set"), so this is the first thing that would need one — weigh that against a simpler shape before adding it.
- Does it interact with isExerciseDone, or sit beside it? isExerciseDone is shared by two screens precisely so they cannot disagree; whatever is added must keep that property.
- Should finishing early with ZERO logged sets be allowed (a skip)? That is arguably a different verb — "skipped" vs "finished short" — and the distinction matters for any future adherence or volume stat.
- Does an early finish advance focus the way completing the last set does (completeSet / pickNextInGroup), and does it advance the rotation on StartScreen?
- Is it reversible? Tapping again should un-finish, since the two-tap armed-confirm pattern (DELETE_ARM_MS) is already the house style for destructive-ish taps.

UI: likely a control on the active card near the pips or the Complete-set button. Reuse the armed-confirm shape rather than a modal, per CLAUDE.md.

FILES: apps/web/src/screens/session/SessionScreen.tsx (active card, completeSet, focus derivation), wherever isExerciseDone lives, apps/web/src/screens/StartScreen (rotation advance), apps/api/src/routes/sessions.ts and the schema if a flag needs persisting.
title: Finish an exercise early without logging every set
